description.p: CoreX is a lightweight hardware monitor for Linux that keeps you informed about your system's health at all times.

ul.li: Every sensor of your PC in one list: CPU and GPU temperatures, fan speeds, voltages, power, clocks, disks and network, each with its minimum and maximum
A dashboard with live charts per device, or charts only for the values you pick
An always-on-top widget with the values you choose, visible while gaming, working or browsing
A widget editor: place every value where you want it, add icons, pick text sizes, the widget size, the background opacity and your own background image
History of every sensor for up to a year, with charts and CSV export
Alerts above or below any value, with a desktop notification
A system report of your hardware and readings, ready to paste in a forum post
Dark, light or system theme
Rename sensors, hide the ones you do not need; CoreX remembers your layout
Can start with your system, straight into the widget
Light on resources: it reads the kernel directly, no background services

screenshot.caption: Every sensor in one list, charts on demand

ul.li: Widget editor: free placement of every value, icons, text sizes, widget size, background opacity and background image
Move the widget with Ctrl + drag, lock its position
History of every sensor (last hour to 30 days, kept up to a year) with CSV export
Alerts above or below any value, with a desktop notification
System report to copy or save
Dark, light or system theme
Icons on the sensor groups
New sensor engine: accurate network and disk rates, NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs, NVMe and drive temperatures
Choose how you see CoreX: List, List with widget, or Dashboard
Minimum and maximum for every sensor, rename and hide sensors
Start with system
